title: To and from
intro: [A1 unit 5](a1-u05) said where things **are**. This unit says where they **go** and where they **come from**: the dative `-A` (to, toward), the ablative `-dAn` (from, out of), and the same two cases on the pronouns and on the question words: *maňa* (to me), *menden* (from me), *nirä* (where to).

blocks.text: To say where someone or something is going, add `-A` to the noun: *-a* after a back vowel, *-e* after a front one, by vowel harmony as in [A1 unit 2](a1-u02). Grammars call this ending the dative. It does the work of English **to**, **toward** and **into**: *öý* (house) → *öýe* (home, to the house), *bazar* → *bazara* (to the market).

blocks.label: The dative after a consonant
lines: -A  →  -e   after e, ä, i, ö, ü

blocks.text: Ask **where to** with *nirä*: *Nirä barýarsyň?* Where are you going? The answer is often just the place: *Öýe.* Home.

items.en: Where are you going? — To Dashoguz.
The guests are coming to the city.

blocks.text: **barmak, gitmek, gelmek.** *barmak* means **to go to** a place, to get there; it nearly always has a place in the dative. *gitmek* (to go, to leave) can stand alone: *Men gidýärin*, I'm leaving. *gelmek* is **to come**. With a destination, *barmak* and *gitmek* are both fine: *Öýe barýaryn* and *Öýe gidýärin* both mean I'm going home.

blocks.title: Where, or where to
blocks.text: *öýde* is **at** home; *öýe* is **to** home. *Men öýde* (I'm at home), but *Men öýe barýaryn* (I'm going home). In the same way, *nirede* asks **where** and *nirä* asks **where to**.

**After a vowel the ending merges with the word.** Turkmen adds no second vowel and no *ý*: the last vowel of the word itself becomes the ending. A final *a* or *y* becomes *a*; a final *e* or *i* becomes *ä*. A word that ends in *a* therefore looks the same in the dative: *oba* means both **village** and **to the village**, and the sentence tells you which.

blocks.label: The dative after a vowel
lines: final a, y  →  a     oba, Mara
final e, i  →  ä     ejä, kişä

items.en: The teacher is looking at the pupil.

blocks.title: Not Marya, not ejeýe
blocks.text: Never add anything after the final vowel: *Mara*, not *Marya*; *ejä*, not *ejeä* or *ejeýe*; *okuwça*, not *okuwçya*. And keep *e* and *ä* apart: *eja* is wrong too, because *eje* has front vowels.

**k, p, ç soften before the dative.** When a word of two or more syllables ends in *k*, *p* or *ç*, that consonant turns into *g*, *b* or *j* before the vowel of the ending: *mekdep* → *mekdebe* (to school), *sapak* → *sapaga* (to the lesson). The name *Aşgabat* does the same with its *t*: *Aşgabada*. [A1 unit 8](a1-u08) explains this softening in full; for now, learn these three.

items.en: The children are going to school.
The students are coming to the lesson.

blocks.text: **Verbs that take the dative.** Several verbs that English joins to **at**, **for**, **in** or nothing at all take the dative in Turkmen. Learn them with the case.

head: Verb
Meaning
Example
rows: *Surata seredýärin.* I'm looking at the picture.
*Awtobusa garaşýarys.* We're waiting for the bus.
*Awtobusa münýäris.* We're getting on the bus.

blocks.title: One ending for many little words
blocks.text: English says look **at**, wait **for**, believe **in**. Turkmen uses the dative for all of them, so you never need to choose a preposition: *surata seretmek*, *awtobusa garaşmak*.

To say where something comes **from**, add `-dAn`: *-dan* after a back vowel, *-den* after a front one. This is the ablative. It works like the locative of [A1 unit 5](a1-u05): the *d* never changes, nothing merges, and the word keeps its last letter: *mekdepden*, *Aşgabatdan*, *Marydan*, *ejeden*.

blocks.label: The ablative
lines: -dAn  →  -den   after e, ä, i, ö, ü

items.en: Aýna is going out of the house.
Where are you from? — I'm from London.
The school isn't far from home.

blocks.text: **Where are you from?** *Siz nireden?* asks the same as *Siz nireli?* from [A1 unit 3](a1-u03), and the answer can use either ending: *Men Londondan* or *Men Londonly*.

**Verbs that take the ablative.** *çykmak* (to go out, to come out) and *düşmek* (to get off, to come down) take the place you leave: *Öýden çykýaryn*, I'm going out of the house; *Awtobusdan düşýärin*, I'm getting off the bus. *gorkmak* (to be afraid) takes what you fear: *Men uçardan gorkýaryn*, I'm afraid of planes. *uzak* (far) and *ýakyn* (near) take the place they are far from or near to: *Bazar bu ýerden ýakyn*, The market is near here.

items.en: The pupils aren't afraid of the teacher.
Myrat is getting off the bus.

blocks.text: **From … to: -dan … -a çenli.** *çenli* means **up to, as far as**. Put the starting point in the ablative and the end point in the dative before *çenli*: *Aşgabatdan Mara çenli*, from Ashgabat to Mary.

items.en: The road from Ashgabat to Mary is long.
It isn't far from home to school.

blocks.title: mekdebe, but mekdepden
blocks.text: Only a vowel softens *k*, *p* and *ç*. The ablative starts with a consonant, so the word keeps its letter: *mekdepden*, *Aşgabatdan*. Compare the dative: *mekdebe*, *Aşgabada*.

sections.title: To me, from me: pronouns and question words

blocks.text: The pronouns take the same two cases. In the ablative they are regular. In the dative, *men*, *sen* and *ol* change: *maňa*, *saňa*, *oňa*, with *ň* (the *ng* of *sing*). *ol* takes the extra *n* you met in *onda*: *ondan*.

**Where to, where from.** The question words *nire* and *kim* and the words for here and there take the cases like any noun. *nire* (which place) is only used with an ending: *nirede*, *nirä*, *nireden*.

items.en: Where are you going? — To the market.
Where are you coming from? — From work.

blocks.text: **Right and left.** *sag* is **right** and *çep* is **left**. With the locative they say where something is, with the dative where it goes: *Dükan sagda*, the shop is on the right; *Ýol çepe gidýär*, the road goes to the left.

blocks.title: Going to see someone
blocks.text: To visit someone, Turkmen usually puts the plural on the name, as if the whole household were meant: *Merdanlara barýarys*, we're going to Merdan's. A grammar of Turkmen on the SIL dictionary site warns that a person in the dative with *gelmek* can mean something else: a woman who **comes to** a man marries him.

summary: The dative `-A` says **to** or **toward**: *öýe*, *işe*, *bazara*. Ask with *nirä*.
After a vowel it merges with the word: final *a*, *y* → *a* (*oba*, *Mara*, *okuwça*); final *e*, *i* → *ä* (*ejä*, *kişä*). Never *Marya*.
Before the dative, *k*, *p*, *ç* of a longer word soften: *mekdebe*, *sapaga*; and *Aşgabada*.
The ablative `-dAn` says **from** or **out of**, always with *d*, nothing merges: *işden*, *Marydan*, *mekdepden*. *gorkmak*, *çykmak* and *düşmek* take it.
Pronouns: *maňa, saňa, oňa, bize, size, olara*; *menden, senden, ondan, bizden, sizden, olardan*. Places: *nirä, nireden, bu ýere, bu ýerden*.
